problems.title: Double-angle cosine from tangent
problems.question: Given tanα=1/2, find cos2α.
problems.idea: Divide the cosine double-angle identity by sin²α+cos²α to express it through tangent.
steps: The given tangent is defined, so cosα≠0 and the tangent form applies.
Substitute tan²α=1/4.

problems.title: Use fourth powers to find a double-angle sine
problems.question: α∈(π,3π/2) and sin⁴α+cos⁴α=2/3. Find sin2α.
problems.idea: Expand the square of sin²α+cos²α, then determine the sign from the quadrant.
steps: The given equation gives 2sin²αcos²α=1/3.
Thus sin²2α=4sin²αcos²α=2/3.
In quadrant III, both sinα and cosα are negative, so sin2α is positive.
Take the positive root: sin2α=√(2/3)=√6/3.

problems.title: A half-angle tangent with quadrant control
problems.question: Find tan(x/4) if sin(x/2)=-0.8 and 360°<x<540°.
problems.idea: First locate x/2 and find its cosine. Then apply a half-angle identity.
formulas: tan(θ/2)=sinθ/(1+cosθ) when the denominator is nonzero.
steps: Let θ=x/2. Then 180°<θ<270°, so cosine is negative.
sinθ=-4/5 gives cosθ=-3/5.
The sign is also consistent with x/4 lying in quadrant II.

problems.title: Prove an identity using angle differences
problems.question: Prove $(\cos4\tan2-\sin4)/(\cos4\cot2+\sin4)=-\tan^22$. Angles without degree signs are in radians.
problems.idea: Put each part over sin2 or cos2; their numerators become angle-difference identities.
formulas: sin(u-v)=sin u cos v-cos u sin v.
cos(u-v)=cos u cos v+sin u sin v.
tan t=sin t/cos t; cot t=cos t/sin t.
steps: The numerator becomes (cos4·sin2-sin4·cos2)/cos2=sin(2-4)/cos2=-sin2/cos2=-tan2.
The denominator becomes (cos4·cos2+sin4·sin2)/sin2=cos(4-2)/sin2=cos2/sin2=cot2.
The quotient is (-tan2)/cot2=-tan²2.
At the fixed radian angle 2, both sine and cosine are nonzero, so these divisions are allowed.

problems.title: Simplify a product containing reciprocal cosine
problems.question: Simplify $\dfrac{(\tan x+\cos^{-1}x)(\cos x-\cot x)}{(\cos x+\cot x)(\tan x-\cos^{-1}x)}$, where cos⁻¹x means 1/cosx.
problems.idea: Rewrite everything using s=sinx and c=cosx, then compare numerator and denominator.
steps: The original expression requires s≠0 and c≠0. These also exclude s=±1, so the remaining denominator factors are nonzero.
The numerator is ((s+1)/c)·(c(s-1)/s)=(s²-1)/s.
The denominator is (c(s+1)/s)·((s-1)/c)=(s²-1)/s.
The two nonzero expressions are equal, so their ratio is 1.
problems.note: The source uses a negative exponent on cosine to mean a reciprocal, not the inverse function arccos.

problems.title: Range of a quadratic in sine
problems.question: Find the range of y=3cos²x+sinx-1.
problems.idea: Put t=sinx, keeping -1≤t≤1. Find the vertex maximum and compare endpoint minima.
steps: The expression becomes 2+t-3t² for t∈[-1,1].
The completed square gives a maximum 25/12 at t=1/6, which is attainable.
The downward-opening quadratic has its minimum on this interval at an endpoint. At t=-1 its value is -2; at t=1 it is 0.
Continuity gives every value between the minimum and maximum.

problems.title: Construct a plane section of a rectangular box
problems.question: In rectangular box ABCDA1B1C1D1, M is on edge BB1 and N on edge CD. Construct the section by plane AMN.
problems.idea: Intersect the cutting plane with successive faces. The front and back face planes are parallel.
formulas: If a plane cuts two parallel planes, their intersection lines are parallel.
The intersection of a plane with a convex box is a convex polygon.
steps: Draw AM on front face ABB1A1. Draw AN on the bottom face ABCD.
On the back face DCC1D1, draw through N the line parallel to AM. Its intersection with edge CC1 is K.
Join K to M on right face BCC1B1, and K to N on the back face.
The boundary is A-M-K-N-A. To check existence, use A=(0,0,0), B=(a,0,0), D=(0,b,0), M=(a,0,m), N=(n,b,0), with 0<m<h and 0<n<a.
The cutting plane is z=(m/a)x-(mn/(ab))y. At CC1 it has height m(1-n/a), strictly between 0 and h; it never reaches the top face. This confirms the four sides.
problems.answer: The section is quadrilateral AMKN, with AM∥NK.
problems.note: This construction assumes M and N lie inside their edges, as usual. Endpoint positions give limiting triangles or coincident vertices.

problems.title: Distance to a plane from a dihedral angle
problems.question: AC is a leg of right triangle ABC and lies in plane w. The planes ABC and w make 30°. If AC=8 and AB=3BC, find B’s distance to w.
problems.idea: The right angle must be at C. Then BC is the perpendicular distance from B to the hinge line AC within its own plane.
formulas: Distance to the other plane=(distance to the hinge)·sin(dihedral angle).
steps: AB cannot be a leg when AB=3BC and BC is the hypotenuse. Hence AB is the hypotenuse and ∠C=90°.
Let BC=t. Then (3t)²=8²+t², so 8t²=64 and t=2√2.
In the cross-section perpendicular to AC, the two planes make 30°. The required distance is BC·sin30°=2√2·1/2=√2.

problems.title: Distance from an equidistant point to a triangle side
problems.question: M is outside the plane of triangle ABC, MA=MB=MC, AB=AC=4, BC=6, and M is 2 units from the plane. Find distance(M,BC). The source also offers an alternative dihedral-angle problem; it is explained below.
problems.idea: Project M to the triangle’s circumcentre O. Then combine its height with O’s distance to BC.
formulas: For the main problem: squared distances add in perpendicular directions.
For the alternative: sinθ=sinα·sinβ, hence cosθ=√(1-sin²α sin²β).
steps: Main problem: choose B=(-3,0), C=(3,0), and A=(0,√7) in the triangle’s plane, since its altitude is √(4²-3²)=√7.
Equal distances force O=(0,u). Equate OB²=OA²: 9+u²=(√7-u)², giving u=-1/√7. Thus O is outside the triangle, 1/√7 from line BC.
The closest point on BC is its midpoint, and distance(M,BC)=√(2²+(1/√7)²)=√(29/7).
Alternative question: a line AB in one face of a dihedral angle α passes through B on the hinge and makes angle β with the hinge. Find the cosine of its angle θ to the other face.
If AB=L, its component in the first face perpendicular to the hinge has length Lsinβ. Rotating across the dihedral angle gives normal height Lsinβ sinα above the second face.
Therefore sinθ=|sinβ sinα|. Since a line-plane angle lies between 0° and 90°, its cosine is the nonnegative square root √(1-sin²α sin²β).

problems.title: Distance across two faces of a dihedral angle
problems.question: A,B lie on the respective faces of a dihedral angle α. Their perpendicular feet on the hinge are A1,B1, with AA1=2, BB1=3, A1B1=5, and cosα=1/3. Find AB.
problems.idea: Separate the displacement along the hinge from the perpendicular cross-section displacement.
steps: The component parallel to the hinge has length 5.
In a perpendicular cross-section, the two face directions make angle α. The squared transverse separation is 2²+3²-2·2·3·(1/3)=9.
The hinge direction is perpendicular to the cross-section, so AB²=25+9=34.
Take the positive root for the distance.
